title: Stored sample can be linked back to a specific individual via labels or metadata
description: When the wet lab sends a physical sample into freezer storage, identifiers on the tube, rack position records, or associated inventory metadata may permit direct or indirect linkage of the stored sample to a specific person.
assumptions: Stored physical samples are labeled and indexed in an inventory system or freezer log.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping for storage/indexing of a physical sample; sub-activity id may be approximate.

title: Presence of a person's sample in storage may be inferable
description: If freezer contents, storage manifests, or access records are visible to unauthorized parties, they may infer that a given individual has provided a sample, revealing participation in a study, treatment, or testing activity.
assumptions: Some parties can observe freezer labels, manifests, or inventory/access records beyond strict need-to-know.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity chosen as a best-effort fit for placing/retaining a sample in storage; exact id may differ.

title: Sample may be retained or repurposed beyond the individual's expectations or consent
description: Once placed into long-term freezer storage, the physical sample may be kept longer than necessary or reused for additional purposes not covered by the original consent or notice.
assumptions: Retention and secondary-use controls are not strictly enforced for stored samples.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping for storage/retention activity; exact PANOPTIC sub-activity id is uncertain.

title: Stored sample and related freezer records may disclose excessive sensitive information
description: The physical sample itself, combined with labels or associated storage metadata, can expose more personal or sensitive information than necessary, such as identity, health status, or membership in a sensitive cohort, if seen or accessed improperly.
assumptions: Samples or storage records carry rich metadata or are accessible to personnel who do not need full detail.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node selection is best-effort given the physical-sample storage context; PANOPTIC sub-activity id may be approximate.

title: Wet lab can link de-identified sample ID back to identifiable context
description: Even though the LIMS returns a de-identified ID, the wet lab may already possess local context, timing, handling notes, or specimen logistics that allow the de-identified ID to be linked back to a person or collection event. This undermines the intended separation between direct identifiers and laboratory handling.
assumptions: Wet lab staff or systems retain auxiliary information about sample collection, intake timing, or order context that can be combined with the returned ID.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping for pseudonymized identifier assignment/use; exact sub-activity id is uncertain.

title: LIMS may disclose pseudonymous identifier to an unintended recipient or channel
description: If the de-identified ID is sent to the wrong wet lab system instance, wrong workstation, or over an inadequately protected channel, the identifier and associated sample metadata may be exposed beyond the intended processing context. While the ID is de-identified, it still concerns a specific sample and may be sensitive when combined with other data.
assumptions: The flow traverses infrastructure where routing errors, access-control weaknesses, or transmission exposure are possible.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity is a best-effort choice for transmitting sample metadata/identifier; exact id may differ.

title: De-identified ID may be insufficiently protected against guessing or reversal
description: If the generated de-identified ID is predictable, encodes meaningful attributes, or is derived from source identifiers using a reversible or weak transformation, recipients or insiders may infer original identifiers or sensitive attributes from it. This weakens de-identification and may expose information unnecessarily.
assumptions: The de-identified ID scheme may embed structure, sequence, or transformation artifacts rather than being random and non-semantic.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping for identifier generation/assignment; exact sub-activity id is uncertain.

title: Lack of evidence about receipt and use of the de-identified ID
description: If the transfer is not logged with sufficient provenance, the wet lab may be unable to prove which de-identified ID was received for a given sample or whether it used the correct identifier. This can hinder investigations into mislabeling, privacy incidents, or improper relinking.
assumptions: Audit trails for outbound and inbound metadata exchange are incomplete, mutable, or not correlated across systems.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC mapping is approximate; this is primarily a non-repudiation/provenance concern around the transmission event.

title: Unclear handling rules may enable use of the de-identified ID beyond the intended purpose
description: The wet lab may not have enough context about the allowed uses, retention, or onward sharing of the de-identified ID. If purpose limitation and handling constraints are not communicated with the flow, the ID can be reused in broader contexts than intended, increasing re-identification and secondary-use risk.
assumptions: No explicit machine-readable or procedural policy accompanies the identifier indicating permitted use, retention, or disclosure limits.
uncertainty_note: PA03.09 is a best-effort PANOPTIC guess for communicating privacy constraints/purpose context; exact sub-activity id is uncertain.

title: Wet lab personnel may be unaware that the returned ID remains personal data in context
description: Because the identifier is described as de-identified, staff may incorrectly treat it as non-sensitive. In context, however, it may still be reasonably linkable to an individual or specimen. This can lead to insufficient safeguards, inappropriate sharing, or over-retention.
assumptions: Operational users rely on the label 'de-identified' without considering contextual re-identification risk.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC mapping is approximate for identifier use/handling awareness rather than a discrete system action.

title: Raw sequence data stored in identifiable form on cluster filesystem
description: Digital raw sequence data may be directly or indirectly identifiable to a data subject, and storing it on the cluster filesystem can expose identity if file contents, filenames, paths, or associated metadata retain sample identifiers or links to subject records.
assumptions: The raw sequence data or its storage metadata can be linked to an individual or donor, either directly or via project/sample identifiers.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity id is best-effort based on storing/persisting data; exact mapping may vary.

title: Linkability of sequence files across projects or processing runs
description: Persisting raw sequence data in a shared cluster filesystem may allow files, sample IDs, directory structures, timestamps, or storage metadata to be linked across studies, runs, or collaborators, enabling correlation of records that should remain separate.
assumptions: The filesystem is multi-user or supports shared administrative/analysis access, and identifiers or metadata are reused across contexts.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity id is approximate for storage; tree node is best-effort for cross-context linking.

title: Inference of sensitive traits from stored raw genomic sequence data
description: Even if explicit identifiers are removed, stored raw genomic sequence data can permit inference of sensitive health, ancestry, kinship, or other personal attributes when accessed or analyzed later.
assumptions: The sequence data is human or otherwise tied to an identifiable person and is retained in sufficiently rich form for downstream analysis.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity id is best-effort for persistent storage of analyzable data.

title: Detectability of presence of a subject or sample through filesystem artifacts
description: The existence of specific raw sequence files, filenames, directory entries, timestamps, quotas, or job/storage logs may reveal that sequencing occurred for a particular subject, cohort, or condition, even without reading file contents.
assumptions: Adversaries or unauthorized insiders can observe some filesystem metadata, logs, or naming conventions.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity id is approximate; this threat focuses on storage-side metadata visibility.

title: Unawareness of long-term storage and downstream reuse of raw sequence data
description: Data subjects may be unaware that their raw sequence data is being stored on a cluster filesystem for extended periods and may later be reused for analysis, sharing, backup, or secondary purposes beyond the original wet-lab generation context.
assumptions: Notice to subjects is incomplete or does not clearly describe this storage and subsequent use context.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity id is best-effort; exact PANOPTIC mapping for user awareness/notice may differ from storage action.

title: Storage of raw sequence data beyond consented or authorized purposes
description: Sending and storing raw sequence data on the cluster filesystem may exceed the purposes, retention limits, access restrictions, or governance conditions originally agreed with the data subject or required by policy.
assumptions: Consent, legal basis, or internal policy imposes purpose limitation, retention, or access constraints on genomic data storage.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity id is approximate for storage activity; exact non-compliance node may vary by applicable policy/regulatory context.

title: Compute-node processing can expose sensitive sequence data beyond the intended analysis purpose
description: Raw digital sequence data sent from the cluster filesystem to compute nodes may be read or used by jobs, users, or services on those nodes for purposes other than the stated transformation into objective-specific data. Because sequence data can contain highly sensitive, potentially identifying genetic information, use on shared compute infrastructure can create a privacy risk if purpose limitation is not technically enforced.
assumptions: Compute nodes are multi-tenant or accessible by multiple jobs, users, or services; raw sequence data contains personal or human-derived genomic information or similarly sensitive biological data.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity is best-effort: mapped to a generic processing/use-of-data activity because the exact PANOPTIC action for analytical transformation of sequence data is uncertain without the reference taxonomy.

title: Processing raw sequence data on compute nodes can reveal identities or enable re-identification
description: Even if direct identifiers are absent, raw sequence data transferred to compute nodes may itself be inherently identifying or linkable. Analysts, co-resident workloads, or system components with access to the data during processing could infer or re-identify the underlying individual(s), especially when combined with metadata or reference datasets.
assumptions: The sequence data is person-related or can be linked to individuals; compute environments expose data to operators, logs, temporary storage, memory snapshots, or other workloads.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC action assignment; exact sub-activity id for analysis/processing of sequence data may differ.

title: Transfer of sequence data from storage to compute nodes may enable linkage across analyses or datasets
description: When the same raw sequence data is repeatedly retrieved from the cluster filesystem and processed on compute nodes, internal identifiers, filenames, paths, sample IDs, or stable dataset handles can allow observers or platform components to link separate runs, projects, or subjects together. This may reveal relationships between datasets and research objectives that were not intended to be exposed.
assumptions: Stable identifiers or metadata accompany the transferred files; observers can see job context, file paths, or transfer metadata.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity id is approximate and based on a generic data transfer/collection interpretation.

title: Compute processing may derive new sensitive attributes from raw sequence data
description: Transformation of raw sequence data into objective-specific outputs can generate inferred traits, variants, ancestry, disease propensity, or other derived personal information beyond what data subjects reasonably expect. These derived results may increase sensitivity even if the original transfer was for a narrower analytical purpose.
assumptions: The processing pipeline derives biologically meaningful features or analytics from raw sequence data that relate to individuals or groups.
uncertainty_note: Exact PANOPTIC sub-activity for inference/derivation is uncertain; chosen id is best-effort for processing/transformation.

title: Insufficient proof of authorized disclosure from the cluster filesystem to compute nodes
description: If the filesystem-to-compute transfer lacks robust provenance and access-record evidence, it may be difficult later to demonstrate that only authorized jobs or users accessed the raw sequence data. This weakens accountability for disclosures of highly sensitive sequence data.
assumptions: Audit trails for file reads, job identity, and transfer authorization may be incomplete, mutable, or not strongly bound to the requesting process.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity id is approximate for the act of making data available/transferring it from storage to processing.

title: Data subjects may be unaware that raw sequence data is processed on shared compute infrastructure
description: The movement of raw sequence data from storage to compute nodes for transformation may be opaque to data subjects or data contributors. If notices, consent materials, or governance records do not clearly cover this operational use, individuals may not understand where and how their highly sensitive sequence data is being processed.
assumptions: The data concerns identifiable or potentially identifiable individuals and transparency obligations apply.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping to a generic processing activity; exact transparency-related PANOPTIC sub-activity is uncertain.

title: Transfer of research data to DMZ may expose sensitive attributes beyond intended delivery scope
description: Moving context-relevant research data from the cluster filesystem into the data delivery DMZ can disclose personal or otherwise sensitive research data to systems, operators, or delivery channels with broader exposure than the originating environment. If the dataset is insufficiently minimized, filtered, or access-scoped before transfer, recipients or intermediaries may learn more than necessary.
assumptions: The research data may contain personal data or indirectly identifying data, and the DMZ is more exposed or accessible than the source storage environment.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping for a data transfer/disclosure step; exact sub-activity id may differ.

title: Data made available in the delivery DMZ may enable identification of data subjects
description: Once generated research data is staged in the data delivery DMZ for delivery, direct identifiers, quasi-identifiers, metadata, or unique combinations of attributes may allow users of the DMZ or downstream recipients to identify individual data subjects, especially when combined with external information.
assumptions: Delivered research data is not guaranteed to be fully anonymized and may retain identifying or linkable elements.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity is a best-effort estimate for staging/transferring data for disclosure.

title: Staged delivery data in the DMZ may be linkable with other datasets
description: Research data copied into the data delivery DMZ may include stable pseudonyms, consistent record structures, timestamps, project metadata, or other quasi-identifiers that allow correlation with prior deliveries or external datasets. This can let an observer link records across contexts and build richer profiles.
assumptions: The same or similar subjects may appear in multiple datasets or releases, and the DMZ supports repeated or multi-party data delivery.
uncertainty_note: Tree node chosen at a high level because exact applicable LINDDUN Pro child node depends on detailed schema and release model.

title: Publishing data in the delivery DMZ may reveal sensitive facts about individuals
description: Even where direct identifiers are removed, the content of context-relevant research data may disclose confidential characteristics, conditions, behaviors, locations, or participation in sensitive studies once made available through the DMZ. This is especially relevant if the delivery environment is reachable by a wider audience or if authorization is weak.
assumptions: The research data content itself may contain sensitive or inferentially sensitive information.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC and high-level LINDDUN node selection; specific disclosure mode depends on dataset content and DMZ access controls.

title: Use of a DMZ for delivery may exceed the original purpose or consent context
description: Copying research data into a delivery DMZ for dissemination may create a new processing context that is broader than the purpose, legal basis, consent, or sharing expectations under which the data was originally generated and stored. If secondary recipients or broader delivery mechanisms are enabled, the data subjects may not have meaningful control over this onward sharing.
assumptions: Purpose limitation, consent constraints, or sharing restrictions may apply to the research dataset.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC action is inferred from the transfer-for-delivery context rather than from an explicit provided action catalog.

title: Insufficient evidence of authorized transfer to the DMZ can weaken accountability for disclosures
description: If the transfer of research data from the cluster filesystem into the delivery DMZ is not strongly logged with dataset version, authorizing actor, purpose, and recipient context, parties may later be unable to prove what was disclosed, to whom, and under what authority. This undermines auditability of privacy-relevant disclosures.
assumptions: Logging and provenance controls for DMZ staging may be incomplete or not tamper-evident.
uncertainty_note: This is an accountability/repudiation-oriented privacy threat inferred from the delivery workflow; PANOPTIC id is best-effort.

title: Unawareness of sample-request processing and downstream transfer
description: The requested donor's physical sample may be prepared for release and sent to a sequencing lab without the data subject being aware that a researcher-initiated request triggered this specific handling and transfer of their biological material.
assumptions: Assumes sample requests can be fulfilled based on stored specimens linked to identifiable or linkable individuals, and that data subjects are not directly notified of each request and shipment.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping for request-triggered handling/disclosure of a physical specimen; exact sub-activity id may differ.

title: Request exceeds or is incompatible with original consent/authorization
description: A researcher may submit a physical sample request for a use, study scope, or recipient context that is not covered by the donor's original consent, authorization, or applicable governance constraints, creating non-compliance at the point of request.
assumptions: Assumes consent or use restrictions exist for some stored samples and request validation may be incomplete or inconsistent.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC action is a best-effort fit for initiating a collection/access request under constrained authorization; tree node is high-level due to lack of provided node catalog.

title: Excessive disclosure in the physical sample request details
description: The request submitted to the DNA Store may include more personal or sensitive information than necessary to identify and retrieve the specimen, such as unnecessary identifiers, phenotype details, or study context, increasing disclosure risk within the repository workflow.
assumptions: Assumes request forms or messages can carry donor/sample metadata beyond the minimum needed for retrieval and fulfillment.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC mapping is best-effort for over-sharing during a request/transfer workflow; exact sub-activity id may vary.

title: Linkability of donor identity to requested specimen and study
description: The physical sample request can create or reinforce a link between a specific donor/specimen, the requesting researcher, and the intended sequencing activity, enabling inference about the donor's participation or condition across contexts.
assumptions: Assumes the DNA Store maintains identifiers or coded references that can be correlated with researcher, project, or lab information.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC id for linking records across request and fulfillment contexts; exact sub-activity id may differ.

title: Identifiability through specimen request metadata
description: Even if the sample itself is pseudonymous, metadata in the request or repository response may allow the specimen to be tied back to a specific individual through unique sample IDs, rare attributes, or project-specific context.
assumptions: Assumes sample IDs and associated metadata are accessible within the DNA Store workflow and can be combined with other available information.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity id is approximate; identifiability may arise from repository lookup and matching rather than the request message alone.

title: Insufficient proof of authorization or request provenance
description: If the DNA Store cannot reliably demonstrate who submitted the physical sample request, under what approval, and when it was approved, the researcher may later deny making the request or the repository may be unable to prove proper authorization and accountability.
assumptions: Assumes request logging, approval binding, or non-repudiation controls may be weak or fragmented.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping for request submission/provenance recording; exact sub-activity id may differ.

title: Researcher can infer sensitive genetic/health information from the retrieved physical sample
description: When the DNA Store releases the referenced physical sample to the NCCoE Researcher, the sample itself may reveal highly sensitive genetic, familial, ancestry, or health-related information about the data subject once examined or tested. The transfer therefore creates a disclosure risk beyond the mere request metadata.
assumptions: The physical sample is identifiable or linkable to a person and can be analyzed by the receiving researcher.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping for researcher retrieval/access to a stored physical sample; exact sub-activity id may differ.

title: Retrieval of a specific physical sample may enable identification of the data subject
description: By obtaining the referenced physical sample, the NCCoE Researcher may be able to directly identify, or re-identify, the individual associated with the sample through attached labels, chain-of-custody information, or by linking the sample to other records.
assumptions: The sample or accompanying handling context contains direct identifiers, coded identifiers, or linkable metadata.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping for retrieval/access of stored samples; exact sub-activity id is uncertain.

title: Sample retrieval can make the individual linkable across datasets or studies
description: If the physical sample carries persistent identifiers or unique genetic material, the researcher may link this sample to prior collections, study records, or external datasets, enabling correlation of the individual's activities or attributes across contexts.
assumptions: The sample has stable identifiers or intrinsic uniqueness sufficient for matching across contexts.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity is a best estimate for sample access/retrieval; exact id may differ.

title: Sample may be retrieved or used beyond the scope originally consented to by the individual
description: The act of retrieving the physical sample from storage for research may be incompatible with the purpose, permissions, or consent terms under which the sample was originally collected or stored, creating a non-compliance risk.
assumptions: Use restrictions, consent limitations, IRB conditions, or policy constraints apply to the sample.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC action id is uncertain; threat depends on governance and consent conditions not stated in the flow.

title: Insufficient proof of who retrieved which physical sample
description: If retrieval from the DNA Store is not strongly logged with requester identity, sample identifier, time, and authorization basis, the NCCoE Researcher could later deny having retrieved the sample or the organization could be unable to prove the transfer occurred appropriately.
assumptions: Chain-of-custody or audit logging for sample release may be weak or incomplete.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping; exact sub-activity id may differ.

title: The individual may be unaware that their physical sample was retrieved for this research activity
description: Retrieval of the physical sample from storage may occur without the data subject being informed that their specimen is being accessed or reused for this specific research purpose, limiting transparency.
assumptions: No direct notification or transparent access reporting is provided to the individual.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC action id is an informed estimate for sample retrieval/access; exact mapping is uncertain.

title: Sample package enables direct identification of the donor
description: The physical sample or its accompanying paperwork may carry direct identifiers such as name, medical record number, shipping label details, or a unique code that the receiving clerk can readily map to a specific person, allowing identification of the data subject at intake.
assumptions: Assumes the sample is shipped with labels or documents visible to the receiving clerk and that the clerk does not strictly need direct identifiers to perform intake.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping for physical transfer/intake of a sample; sub-activity id may be approximate.

title: Linkability between the physical sample and existing patient or study records
description: Even if the sample uses a study code rather than a direct name, the receiving clerk may be able to link the sample to other manifests, prior shipments, or lab information systems, enabling correlation of the specimen with an individual's broader research or clinical context.
assumptions: Assumes the receiving environment has access to manifests, shipment histories, or local systems that allow code-to-person or code-to-study correlation.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity id is a best-effort estimate for receipt/handling of a physical sample.

title: Unnecessary disclosure of sensitive attributes through sample type or labels
description: The sample type, collection context, visible annotations, or accompanying requisition may reveal sensitive information about the donor, such as disease area, genetic testing purpose, demographic details, or participation in a particular research project, beyond what the receiving clerk needs to know.
assumptions: Assumes sample containers, requisitions, or outer packaging contain context-revealing metadata visible during receipt.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping; exact sub-activity id for physical sample receipt/disclosure may differ.

title: Shipment of excess sample material without data minimization
description: The researcher may send more biological material, supporting paperwork, or contextual metadata than is necessary for sequencing intake, increasing privacy risk if the receiving clerk can access surplus specimen volume or extraneous subject information.
assumptions: Assumes the sequencing lab only needs a subset of the included material or metadata to perform intake and sequencing.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC action and Dd tree node are best-effort because this is a physical-material transfer context.

title: Data subject may be unaware their physical sample is being transferred to an external sequencing lab
description: If notice and consent processes are incomplete or unclear, the individual who provided the sample may not understand that the specimen will be physically shipped to another party for sequencing, undermining predictability and transparency of processing.
assumptions: Assumes the sequencing lab is organizationally distinct from the collector/researcher and that participant notice may not explicitly describe this transfer.
uncertainty_note: This is grounded partly in governance/notice rather than something observable on the flow alone; PANOPTIC id is approximate.

title: Transfer of sample without sufficient legal basis, agreement, or protocol restrictions
description: The physical handoff to the sequencing lab may occur without an appropriate data-use agreement, consent alignment, IRB approval scope, or other policy controls governing external processing of the sample and resulting research data.
assumptions: Assumes the sequencing lab may be a separate entity or processor and that contractual/governance controls are required for compliant transfer.
uncertainty_note: This threat depends on organizational context not fully stated in the flow; PANOPTIC sub-activity id is a best-effort estimate.

title: Patient can infer sensitive condition or testing purpose from the request form
description: The physical sample request form may explicitly reveal the suspected condition, genetic test type, clinic specialty, or other sensitive context to the patient at handoff. This can disclose more information than is necessary at that moment, especially if the patient was not expecting the specific test details or if the form includes extraneous clinical metadata.
assumptions: The request form contains detailed test identifiers, diagnosis codes, or clinician notes rather than a minimal collection instruction.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping: likely a data disclosure/revelation during direct provision of a document to the data subject, but the exact sub-activity id may differ.

title: Sensitive request details may be exposed to bystanders during handoff
description: Because the form is physically handed to the patient, nearby staff, family members, or other patients may see the test name, identifiers, or clinical context on the document, resulting in unauthorized disclosure of personal or health information.
assumptions: The handoff occurs in a shared clinical environment and the form content is visible in plain text.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping: likely disclosure during direct document transfer; exact PANOPTIC sub-activity uncertain.

title: Lack of proof about what information was handed to the patient
description: If the clinic does not record exactly which sample request form version or data fields were provided to the patient, the clinician and organization may later be unable to demonstrate what information was disclosed, what instructions were given, or whether the patient received the correct request.
assumptions: There is no signed acknowledgment, copy retention, or audit trail for the physical handoff.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping only; this is grounded in a physical handoff/document provision event rather than a clearly enumerated PANOPTIC action.

title: Form contents may enable linkability across care contexts
description: If the request form includes persistent identifiers such as full demographics, medical record number, barcode, or accession number, anyone seeing or later obtaining the form may be able to link the patient to other records, visits, or testing events.
assumptions: The form carries stable identifiers that are reused across systems or encounters.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping: likely associated with transferring a document containing identifiers; exact sub-activity id uncertain.

title: Patient may be identifiable from the physical request form
description: The form may include direct identifiers such as name, date of birth, address labels, or contact details that make the patient identifiable to anyone who views or handles it before it reaches the sample collection or sequencing workflow.
assumptions: The physical request form contains direct identifiers in readable form.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping only; exact PANOPTIC sub-activity id uncertain.

title: Clinician can infer sensitive health information from the retrieved physical sample
description: Retrieving and handling a patient's physical sample can reveal special-category health data (e.g., diagnosis, genetics, infectious status) to the clinician beyond what is strictly necessary for the immediate task, especially if the sample is labeled or otherwise directly associated with the patient.
assumptions: The physical sample or its accompanying request contains identifiers or contextual information linking it to the patient and the sample type is itself privacy-revealing.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping only; I am not fully confident that PA03.03 is the exact sub-activity for physical retrieval/access of a sample.

title: Retrieved sample may be linkable to the patient by identifiers or context
description: The physical sample may carry explicit identifiers, labels, barcodes, or unique contextual markers that allow the clinician or others nearby to link the specimen to the specific patient, increasing privacy risk if the linkage is unnecessary or overly exposed during retrieval.
assumptions: The sample container, request form, or storage location includes direct or indirect identifiers.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping only; exact PANOPTIC sub-activity id for specimen retrieval/linkage is uncertain.

title: Use of the physical sample may exceed the patient's consent or expected purpose
description: Once the clinician retrieves the physical sample, it may be used or made available for purposes beyond the specific request the patient understood or consented to, such as additional testing, secondary review, or broader clinical use.
assumptions: Consent or purpose limitation for the sample is narrower than all potential downstream uses after retrieval.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping only; exact PANOPTIC sub-activity id is uncertain because no PANOPTIC reference material was supplied.

title: Sample retrieval may expose patient information to unauthorized parties nearby
description: During physical retrieval, transport, or handoff of the sample, labels or associated paperwork may be visible to unauthorized staff or visitors, causing a disclosure of the patient's identity or health-related information.
assumptions: The retrieval occurs in a shared physical environment where others can observe containers, labels, or accompanying documents.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping only; tree node selected as an approximate fit for unauthorized disclosure in a physical handling context.

title: Sample identity linkability at intake
description: When the receiving clerk accepts the physical sample, labels, requisition forms, barcodes, or accompanying metadata may allow the sample to be linked to a specific individual across clinical and research contexts.
assumptions: The physical sample or its packaging carries direct identifiers, coded identifiers, or stable labels that can be matched with other records.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping: likely relates to collection/receipt and handling of a physical specimen, but the exact sub-activity id may differ.

title: Patient identifiability from sample and paperwork
description: The physical sample and accompanying documentation can directly identify the data subject through names, dates of birth, medical record numbers, or unique specimen identifiers visible to the receiving clerk or others nearby.
assumptions: The sample shipment includes requisition paperwork or labels with direct or quasi-identifiers.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping only; exact PANOPTIC sub-activity id for specimen receipt is uncertain.

title: Disclosure of sensitive health context during physical transfer
description: The type of specimen, clinic origin, test request, or visible annotations on the package may reveal sensitive health or research participation information to unauthorized staff, couriers, or bystanders during handoff to the receiving clerk.
assumptions: Packaging, manifests, or labels expose information about the sample source or purpose.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity id is a best estimate for specimen intake/handling.

title: Unawareness of downstream research-data generation from sample transfer
description: The data subject may not be adequately aware that sending the physical sample to the sequencing lab enables generation of context-relevant research data and potentially further downstream uses beyond immediate clinical handling.
assumptions: Notice and transparency around the transfer and subsequent sequencing/research processing may be incomplete or difficult for the data subject to understand.
uncertainty_note: This is grounded in the transfer enabling downstream processing rather than a visible technical interface; PANOPTIC mapping is approximate.

title: Insufficient proof of consent or authorization associated with the sample
description: If the clinician sends the sample without robust documentation of the patient's consent, authorization, or protocol basis for research-related sequencing, the transfer may later be difficult to verify or contest.
assumptions: The flow supports research-data generation and relies on consent, protocol enrollment, or other authorization that may not be tightly bound to the specimen transfer.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping; exact sub-activity for specimen submission with authorization evidence is uncertain.

title: Use of the sample beyond the patient's expected context
description: Once received by the sequencing lab workflow, the physical sample may be processed for context-relevant research data generation in ways that exceed the patient's original expectations or the stated purpose understood at collection time.
assumptions: Secondary or expanded research use is possible after intake, and expectations/purpose limitations may not be consistently enforced at receipt.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC action is an approximate fit because the risk is tied to intake enabling later context expansion.

title: Unawareness of request-driven secondary use of stored sample data
description: The data store may provide digital sample data in response to a researcher request without the data subject being aware that their stored sample data can be accessed and forwarded for sequencing-related purposes.
assumptions: The digital sample data is linked to identifiable or potentially identifiable individuals and is not purely anonymous.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping; PA03.02 is used here for request/access-related use of stored data, but the exact PANOPTIC sub-activity may differ.

title: Excessive collection in the digital sample request
description: The researcher may include more personal or specimen-linked information in the request than is necessary to retrieve the needed digital sample, enabling over-disclosure from the store.
assumptions: The request can contain participant identifiers, case metadata, or other attributes beyond a minimal lookup key.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity is a best-effort estimate for data submission/request creation rather than a confirmed exact node.

title: Linkability through stable identifiers in the request
description: If the request carries persistent subject, specimen, or study identifiers, it may allow the data store or downstream recipients to link this request with other records or prior requests concerning the same individual or sample.
assumptions: Stable identifiers are present in the request and can be correlated across systems.
uncertainty_note: Tree node selected as best effort for identifier-based linkability on a data flow.

title: Inference of sensitive traits from requested digital sample metadata
description: Even before the sample data is released, the specific request parameters or matching dataset characteristics may reveal sensitive health, genomic, or cohort information about the subject(s) associated with the requested digital sample.
assumptions: The store processes requests against metadata rich enough to imply diagnosis, phenotype, or study participation.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping; exact sub-activity for metadata evaluation/selection may vary.

title: Insufficient evidence of authorization for sample-data release
description: If the data store does not maintain strong proof that the researcher was authorized to request this digital sample, either party may later dispute whether the access and disclosure were legitimate.
assumptions: Request approval, policy checks, or consent/DUA validation may not be strongly bound to the transaction.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort tree-node and PANOPTIC mapping for missing auditable proof around request handling.

title: Request fulfillment beyond consent or policy scope
description: The data store may honor a request for digital sample data that exceeds the permissions granted by participant consent, ethics approval, or data-use policy for sequencing-lab transfer.
assumptions: Consent, IRB, or contractual restrictions exist and are not automatically enforced for each request.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC id is best effort for store-side disclosure/processing in response to a request.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of stored digital sample data during request processing
description: While fulfilling the request, the data store could expose digital sample data to an unauthorized researcher account, overly broad recipient group, or unintended downstream path, resulting in a confidentiality breach.
assumptions: Access control or routing errors are possible during request validation and fulfillment.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping for disclosure during store-side response to a request.

title: Over-disclosure of digital sample data during retrieval
description: When the Digital Sample Data Store returns digital sample data to the NCCoE Researcher, it may disclose more personal or sensitive content than is necessary for the specific request, such as returning full datasets, embedded metadata, or linked records beyond the requested sample scope.
assumptions: The digital sample data may contain personal data, sensitive attributes, or metadata that can affect identifiable individuals.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity is best-effort; I am using a generic retrieve/access action mapping and may not have the exact canonical sub-activity id.

title: Researcher can infer sensitive attributes from retrieved digital sample data
description: Even if the retrieval is authorized, the NCCoE Researcher may learn sensitive characteristics, behavioral patterns, or other private facts about individuals represented in the digital sample data once the data is accessed.
assumptions: The sample data is sufficiently rich to enable learning non-obvious or sensitive information about data subjects.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity is approximate; exact PANOPTIC code for researcher retrieval/access may differ.

title: Re-identification of individuals from digital sample data
description: The NCCoE Researcher may be able to identify or single out individuals in the retrieved digital sample data, especially if quasi-identifiers, unique records, or auxiliary knowledge are available.
assumptions: The data is not fully anonymized or can be combined with other accessible information.
uncertainty_note: Tree node is best-effort for identifiability/singling-out; PANOPTIC sub-activity id is also approximate.

title: Linkability across retrieved sample datasets
description: The researcher may be able to correlate records from the retrieved digital sample data with other datasets, requests, or prior samples, enabling linkage of records that were intended to remain separate.
assumptions: Common identifiers, stable pseudonyms, timestamps, or shared quasi-identifiers exist across datasets.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC action is approximate; exact retrieval/linkage-related sub-activity id may differ.

title: Retrieval incompatible with original collection purpose or consent
description: The Digital Sample Data Store may provide digital sample data to the NCCoE Researcher for a use that is broader than, or incompatible with, the purpose, notice, or consent conditions under which the data was originally collected or prepared.
assumptions: The data is governed by purpose limitations, notices, consent terms, or data-use restrictions.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity id is best-effort; exact code for use/access under a new purpose may differ.

title: Insufficient evidence of researcher access to digital sample data
description: If retrieval events are not adequately logged or bound to the requesting researcher, the researcher may later deny having accessed particular digital sample data, undermining accountability for privacy-relevant use.
assumptions: Audit logging, provenance, or access-record integrity may be incomplete or absent for this flow.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC action is approximate because this is an accountability issue attached to the retrieval step.

title: Linkability of physical sample to a specific individual or donor
description: Labels, barcodes, chain-of-custody forms, or distinctive sample attributes may allow the lab technician to link the received physical sample to a specific person or to other records about that person beyond what is necessary for the research task.
assumptions: The sample or accompanying metadata includes at least one identifier, code, or quasi-identifier that can be associated with an individual.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping for receiving/handling a physical sample with identifying metadata; exact sub-activity id may differ.

title: Identifiability from rich sample metadata or unique specimen characteristics
description: Even if direct identifiers are removed, the physical sample and its accompanying project/context information may contain enough unique characteristics to permit the lab technician to identify the data subject.
assumptions: The sample is rare, contains unique characteristics, or is accompanied by contextual details such as project, collection time, or site.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping; tree-node selection is approximate because the risk arises from both the specimen and its associated context.

title: Excessive disclosure of donor information during sample transfer
description: The receiving clerk may provide more information with the physical sample than the lab technician needs, such as full donor identity, detailed collection context, or unnecessary paperwork, exposing personal data during the handoff.
assumptions: The lab technician does not require all attached information to perform the research task.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping for the transfer/receipt of a physical sample; exact sub-activity id may differ.

title: Unawareness of downstream use enabled by sample handoff
description: The data subject may be unaware that their physical sample is being transferred to a specific lab technician or research project context, creating a risk that processing occurs outside the individual's expectations.
assumptions: Transparency to the data subject about internal transfers and project-specific handling is limited or incomplete.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity is inferred from the transfer/receipt step; exact id is uncertain.

title: Use of sample in a context incompatible with original consent or authorization
description: Transferring the physical sample to a lab technician on the relevant research project may still be incompatible with the original purpose, consent terms, or authorization constraints if the sample is used beyond agreed conditions.
assumptions: The sample is subject to purpose, consent, IRB, or contractual restrictions that may not be fully enforced at transfer time.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping; exact sub-activity id and specific non-compliance node are approximate.

title: Exposure of sensitive personal data if the physical sample is misdelivered or observed in transit
description: Because the asset is a physical sample, loss, misdelivery, or casual observation during the handoff can disclose sensitive health, genetic, or research-participation information to unauthorized persons.
assumptions: The sample container, labels, or accompanying documents reveal personal or sensitive information, or the sample type itself is sensitive.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping for physical transfer; exact PANOPTIC id and disclosure tree node are approximate.

title: Sample label or accompanying identifiers reveal the data subject's identity to wet-lab personnel
description: When the physical sample is transferred, labels, requisition slips, or chain-of-custody materials may include direct identifiers or easily attributable codes, allowing wet-lab staff to identify the individual behind the specimen.
assumptions: The specimen is accompanied by human-readable labels, barcodes, or paperwork that can be linked to a person by the receiving lab.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping for physical transfer/hand-off of a sample; exact sub-activity id may differ.

title: Transferred sample can be linked to other records or prior samples
description: Persistent sample identifiers, accession numbers, or barcode schemes used during hand-off may enable the wet lab to link this specimen to prior submissions, clinical records, or external datasets, increasing identifiability and correlation risk.
assumptions: The receiving process has access to internal or external lookup tables, prior sample history, or shared identifier namespaces.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping; exact PANOPTIC sub-activity for specimen transfer/linkage is uncertain.

title: Excessive subject information is disclosed during sample hand-off
description: More information than necessary for sequencing may accompany the physical sample, such as full name, date of birth, diagnosis, or other contextual details, unnecessarily exposing personal data to wet-lab personnel.
assumptions: Only a minimal accession identifier is required for sequencing, but richer metadata is sent along with the specimen.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping for over-disclosure in specimen transfer; PANOPTIC id may be approximate.

title: Data subject may be unaware their physical sample is being sent onward for sequencing
description: The onward transfer of the physical sample from the lab technician to the wet lab may not be transparent to the individual, reducing awareness of who handles the specimen and for what immediate operational purpose.
assumptions: The subject was not clearly informed that the sample would be routed to a separate wet-lab process or team for sequencing.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity is a best-effort estimate; this threat depends on notice/transparency practices outside the flow itself.

title: Sample is used or routed in a way that exceeds the subject's consent or expected purpose
description: A physical specimen transferred for sequencing may be processed under a broader purpose than the individual consented to or reasonably expected, especially if the sample is later retained or used for additional analyses.
assumptions: Consent or collection notice may be narrower than the operational uses enabled once the wet lab receives the specimen.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping; this is partly contextual and may materialize after receipt rather than during the transfer alone.

title: Insufficient hand-off records make sample transfer non-repudiation and accountability weak
description: If the physical transfer to the wet lab is not logged with clear timestamps, sender/receiver identity, and specimen identifiers, parties may later be unable to prove who handled the sample or when it was transferred, weakening accountability for privacy-impacting events.
assumptions: Chain-of-custody or transfer logging may be incomplete or informal.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node selection is best-effort because LINDDUN non-repudiation variants can be modeled differently for physical chain-of-custody events.

title: Over-disclosure of sensitive genetic findings during counseling session
description: The counselor may disclose more genetic information than is necessary for the patient’s immediate decision-making, such as incidental findings, familial implications, or sensitive risk information not expected by the patient, increasing privacy harm from excessive disclosure.
assumptions: The counseling interaction includes verbal explanation and provision of a results copy, and may cover clinically relevant but highly sensitive findings.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping only; PA03.09 is used as an approximate sub-activity for communicating/interpreting results and recommendations.

title: Counseling content may enable inference about relatives’ genetic traits
description: Explaining interpreted results and recommendations to the patient can reveal or strongly imply hereditary risks concerning biological relatives who have not participated in the interaction, allowing inference of third-party sensitive attributes.
assumptions: The test results involve inherited variants or family-history-based interpretation.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping only; the exact PANOPTIC sub-activity id for disclosure of interpreted hereditary findings may differ.

title: Patient may receive a copy of results in a form that is observable by others
description: Providing the patient with a physical or electronic copy of results during or after counseling may expose the existence and nature of the genetic test to nearby persons, household members, employers, or others if the copy is seen, forwarded, or insufficiently protected.
assumptions: A copy of results is handed over, emailed, portal-delivered, printed, or otherwise made available to the patient.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping only; tree node selection is approximate because detectability can arise from the visible artifact rather than the counseling act itself.

title: Recommendations may be communicated without sufficiently privacy-informed patient choice
description: The patient may feel pressured to accept next steps, sharing, referrals, or downstream uses of genetic information without a clear, freely given, and informed opportunity to limit further disclosure or processing.
assumptions: The session includes discussion of follow-up actions, referrals, or sharing of results beyond the immediate conversation.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping only; PANOPTIC identifier is approximate and this threat depends on how options and consent are actually presented.

title: Insufficient evidence of what privacy explanations and sharing choices were communicated
description: If the counseling conversation and handoff of results are not documented clearly, the organization may later be unable to demonstrate what privacy notices, limitations, or patient choices regarding further sharing were discussed.
assumptions: The flow is part of a broader care process where proof of communicated options and disclosures matters.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping only; applicability depends on whether this conversational exchange is formally recorded.

title: Patient receives results in a setting that exposes sensitive genetic information
description: When interpreted clinical genetic results and recommendations are delivered to the patient, disclosure can occur if the conversation, printed materials, portal message, or email is accessible to family members, caregivers, employers, or others not intended to receive the information. Genetic findings can reveal highly sensitive health and familial information.
assumptions: Results may be communicated verbally, on paper, or through an electronic channel outside a strictly private environment.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping for communicating/providing interpreted results to the data subject; sub-activity id may be approximate.

title: Results and recommendations can identify the patient through uniquely revealing genetic content
description: Even if some obvious identifiers are minimized, the content of interpreted genetic results and associated recommendations can itself be strongly identifying because rare variants, family-history context, or disease associations may single out the patient.
assumptions: The communicated results may contain variant-level detail, pedigree context, or rare-condition information.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping; tree node selected at a high level because the exact applicable identification sub-node depends on model granularity.

title: Interpreted results may enable linkage to relatives or other datasets
description: Genetic interpretations and recommendations may allow linkage between the patient and records about biological relatives, prior tests, research datasets, or insurer/employer-held information. This can expose additional personal information beyond what the patient expects from receiving their own results.
assumptions: The result content includes familial or genotype information that is linkable across contexts.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping; linkage is inferred from the nature of genetic data and may depend on how much detail is included in the communicated results.

title: Patient may not expect or consent to onward inferences embedded in professional recommendations
description: Professional recommendations may incorporate secondary findings, familial implications, reproductive implications, or downstream referrals that go beyond what the patient understood would be conveyed. If this scope is not aligned with the patient's expectations or consent, the communication can create a non-compliance risk.
assumptions: The patient may have consented to testing or counseling under narrower expectations than the full scope of returned findings and recommendations.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping and compliance node; exact non-compliance sub-node depends on the governing consent, notice, and clinical obligations.

title: Patient may be unaware of full privacy implications of the disclosed genetic results
description: Even when results are intentionally provided to the patient, they may not understand the future privacy impact, such as implications for relatives, possible secondary use if they share the report, or risks from storing the information in personal email or devices. This lack of awareness can increase downstream privacy harm.
assumptions: The communication does not fully explain privacy consequences and safe handling expectations.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping; PANOPTIC sub-activity id may be approximate.

title: Excessive disclosure of research data from cluster filesystem to report-generation app
description: The cluster filesystem may provide more context-relevant research data than is necessary for generation of the final clinical report, exposing additional patient or study attributes to the receiving application.
assumptions: The Clinical Result Generation App only needs a subset of the stored dataset to generate the final report.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping for data transfer/disclosure minimization; exact sub-activity id may differ.

title: Linkability of research records within the clinical result generation app
description: When context-relevant research data is ingested by the Clinical Result Generation App, identifiers or stable quasi-identifiers may allow linking records across research datasets and clinical reporting contexts, revealing relationships about the same individual.
assumptions: The incoming data contains direct identifiers, coded identifiers, or a combination of quasi-identifiers usable for correlation.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity is best-effort for data integration/correlation during use of transferred data.

title: Identifiability of data subjects in report-generation processing
description: The Clinical Result Generation App may receive context-relevant research data in a form that permits direct or indirect identification of subjects, even if full identification is not required to create the final clinical report.
assumptions: At least some report-generation steps could operate on pseudonymized, filtered, or otherwise less identifying data.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping; exact sub-activity id uncertain.

title: Use of research data for report generation beyond data-subject expectations
description: Generating a final clinical report from research-context data may represent processing outside the original expectations, permissions, or governance conditions attached to the research dataset, creating a detectability-of-misuse/awareness gap for data subjects.
assumptions: The research data was originally collected under constraints distinct from clinical reporting purposes.
uncertainty_note: LINDDUN classification is best-effort here because this risk can also be framed as non-compliance; PANOPTIC id is approximate.

title: Insufficient evidence of accountable transfer from filesystem to app
description: If the transfer of research data from the cluster filesystem to the Clinical Result Generation App is not adequately logged with purpose, dataset version, requester, and timestamp, actors may later deny that specific sensitive data was disclosed or used for report generation.
assumptions: Audit trails for internal system-to-system data flows may be incomplete or not privacy-specific.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping for transfer/logging activity; exact sub-activity id uncertain.

title: Processing may violate purpose limitation or consent constraints
description: The Clinical Result Generation App may process context-relevant research data to create a clinical report without a lawful basis, compatible purpose assessment, or consent/governance coverage for this specific downstream use.
assumptions: The dataset includes research-derived data whose permitted uses may differ from direct clinical care/reporting.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity is best-effort for downstream use/decision support; exact id may differ.

title: Disclosure of identifiable genetic results to an external prior-enrollment entity
description: The genetic counselor sends patient re-identification results and study-related updates to a 3rd party previous enrollment entity. Because the payload links genetic findings with a specific patient and their study participation, the transfer may expose sensitive health/genetic information to an external party beyond what is strictly necessary.
assumptions: Assumes the transferred results contain directly identifying or readily linkable information and that the recipient is organizationally separate from the counselor's system.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity is best-effort only; PA03.09 is used here to represent external disclosure/sharing of sensitive personal data, but exact sub-activity mapping may differ.

title: Linkability of patient identity with prior study enrollments
description: Once the previous enrollment entity receives the re-identification request and results, it can correlate the patient's identity with records of multiple prior studies. This enables linkage across contexts that may reveal participation patterns or sensitive conditions not apparent within a single study.
assumptions: Assumes the receiving entity maintains records spanning multiple studies or enrollment episodes.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity is approximate; PA04.02 is intended as a best-fit for record correlation/linking across datasets.

title: Inference of sensitive attributes from record updates
description: Updating records based on re-identification results may allow the receiving entity to infer new sensitive attributes about the patient, such as genetic predispositions, disease risk, or family-related implications, even if those attributes were not explicitly known before.
assumptions: Assumes the update contains or implies clinically meaningful genetic findings.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping only; PA05.01 is used to denote inference/derivation of sensitive information from received data.

title: Identifiability created by re-identification update
description: The purpose of the flow is to re-identify a patient in the recipient's records. This directly increases the identifiability of the data subject in records that may previously have been pseudonymous, expanding the set of records that can be tied to a named individual.
assumptions: Assumes some recipient records were previously less directly identifiable or separated from current identifying data.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity is approximate; reused here for the act of sharing data that enables explicit re-identification.

title: Use beyond patient expectations or original enrollment context
description: A previous enrollment entity may update or reuse the patient's records for studies based on the newly provided re-identification results in ways that exceed the purpose originally understood by the patient, especially if the original enrollment context did not clearly cover this downstream updating and cross-study reconciliation.
assumptions: Assumes consent, notice, or contractual terms may not have explicitly covered this specific downstream update and reuse activity.
uncertainty_note: Exact PANOPTIC sub-activity is uncertain; PA06.03 is a best-effort placeholder for secondary use/purpose-extension concerns.

title: Sensitive sequence data may be exposed to unauthorized cluster users
description: Sequence data written from the bioinformaticist to the cluster filesystem could be accessible to other users, administrators, or services on the shared cluster if file permissions, ACLs, or storage isolation are misconfigured. Genomic sequence data can be highly identifying and sensitive.
assumptions: The cluster filesystem is multi-user or administratively accessible beyond the submitting bioinformaticist.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping: this is grounded in storing/persisting data on shared infrastructure; the exact sub-activity id may differ.

title: Sequence data on the cluster filesystem can enable re-identification
description: Even if explicit identifiers are absent, stored sequence data may itself be inherently identifying or linkable with external datasets, allowing an individual or sample donor to be re-identified from the data persisted on the cluster filesystem.
assumptions: The sequence data relates to human or otherwise privacy-sensitive samples and is retained in a form useful for linkage.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping to storage/persistence. Re-identification risk depends strongly on the nature of the sequence data and surrounding controls.

title: Stored sequence data may be linkable across projects or datasets
description: If the same sequence files, sample identifiers, metadata, file paths, or stable storage locations are reused across analyses, observers with access to the cluster filesystem may link records across studies, projects, or time, revealing relationships about the same data subject or sample.
assumptions: Projects share infrastructure, naming conventions, or metadata that permit correlation.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping to storage. Linkability may also arise from metadata rather than the sequence content alone.

title: Excessive retention of sequence data on the cluster filesystem may violate data minimization
description: Sequence data may remain on the cluster filesystem longer than necessary after review, increasing the window for misuse, breach, or policy noncompliance. Temporary review copies, intermediate files, and backups can persist unnoticed.
assumptions: No enforced retention/deletion policy exists for review outputs or raw sequence files on the cluster filesystem.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping to persistence/retention on storage; exact sub-activity id may differ.

title: Use of the cluster filesystem for sequence review may exceed consent or governance constraints
description: Writing and reviewing sequence data on shared research infrastructure could conflict with consent terms, data use agreements, or jurisdictional restrictions if the storage location, administrators, or downstream access are not covered by the permitted processing context.
assumptions: The data is subject to consent, contractual, ethical, or regulatory restrictions.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping to storage/use context. Applicability depends on the governing consent and data use conditions.

title: Insufficient auditability of the bioinformaticist's review actions
description: If the bioinformaticist's access and review of sequence data are not adequately logged, it may be difficult to demonstrate who accessed which sequence files, what checks were performed, and whether privacy-relevant handling was authorized.
assumptions: Audit logging for file access and review activity is incomplete or not routinely preserved.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping to human review/access activity; exact sub-activity id is uncertain.

title: Re-identification risk from insufficient de-identification at sample ID generation
description: When the Wet Lab generates a de-identified sample ID and associated metadata for transfer to LIMS, the chosen identifier scheme may still be linkable to the underlying individual if it embeds meaningful structure, preserves stable cross-context references, or is generated from a weak pseudonymization method. This can allow LIMS users or downstream recipients to infer identity from the supposedly de-identified record.
assumptions: Assumes the generated sample ID is intended to reduce direct identifiability but remains persistent and is used across systems or workflows.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping: PA01.02 is used here for de-identification/pseudonymization activity, but exact sub-activity id may vary.

title: Linkability of de-identified sample records inside LIMS
description: A persistent de-identified sample ID stored in LIMS can enable records about the same sample donor, visit, or related specimens to be linked across projects, time, or operational contexts. Even without direct identifiers, this stable identifier may support profile building or correlation with other datasets.
assumptions: Assumes LIMS stores and reuses the same de-identified ID over time or across multiple modules, studies, or exports.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC action is a best-effort fit for correlation/linking behavior rather than an exact cited mapping.

title: Detectability of sensitive sample events through metadata patterns
description: Even if names are removed, the metadata and generated de-identified ID may reveal that a specific sample or patient event exists in LIMS, especially if identifiers are sequential, timestamp-derived, site-coded, or otherwise patterned. An observer could detect the presence of a particular case, sample type, or collection event from the identifier issuance pattern alone.
assumptions: Assumes authorized or unauthorized observers can view identifier formats, sequence ranges, or related metadata in LIMS.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping to the de-identification step; exact sub-activity id uncertain.

title: Disclosure from combining de-identified sample metadata with other LIMS data
description: Once received by LIMS, ostensibly de-identified sample metadata may be combined with operational details such as collection time, location, assay type, technician assignment, or rare specimen attributes. This combination can disclose the data subject's identity or sensitive attributes despite the use of a de-identified ID.
assumptions: Assumes LIMS contains auxiliary data or supports queries that let users combine the incoming metadata with other records.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC action is best-effort for downstream correlation/combination leading to disclosure; exact sub-activity id may differ.

title: Insufficient auditability of de-identified ID generation
description: If the Wet Lab does not maintain controlled evidence of how a de-identified sample ID was generated, mapped, and transmitted, it may be impossible to later demonstrate whether privacy-preserving generation rules were followed or whether an incorrect identifier exposed patient information. This weakens accountability for privacy-relevant processing.
assumptions: Assumes identifier generation or transmission may occur through manual or weakly logged steps.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping to the identifier-generation activity; exact PANOPTIC sub-activity uncertain.

title: Excessive exposure of research data in DMZ retrieval area
description: Making context-relevant research data available in a DMZ for retrieval can disclose personal or sensitive research information to parties beyond the intended NCCoE-trusted recipient if access controls, segmentation, or object scoping are too broad.
assumptions: The research data may contain personal or linkable information and the DMZ repository is reachable by more than one system or user principal.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping for making data available for recipient retrieval; exact PANOPTIC sub-activity id may differ.

title: Recipient retrieval enables linkability across research deliveries
description: If the trusted recipient retrieves multiple datasets or repeated deliveries using stable identifiers, paths, tokens, or account context, the recipient or observers may be able to link records and delivery events relating to the same data subjects or study participants across releases.
assumptions: Retrieval uses persistent identifiers, filenames, account IDs, or delivery metadata that remain stable over time.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC action is a best-fit estimate for delivery/retrieval availability rather than a certain citation.

title: Retrieval metadata may reveal subject or study involvement
description: Even if payload contents are protected, filenames, folder names, URLs, timestamps, and delivery notices associated with recipient retrieval may allow inference that specific individuals, organizations, or studies are involved in the research data exchange.
assumptions: Observable metadata includes meaningful study names, participant codes, project identifiers, or timing correlated with real-world events.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping; exact sub-activity id uncertain.

title: Insufficient proof of what research data was made available
description: If the DMZ does not keep reliable, integrity-protected logs of what data objects were published, when, and for which recipient, the sender or recipient could later dispute what was actually delivered or exposed for retrieval, weakening accountability for privacy-relevant disclosures.
assumptions: Audit records may be absent, mutable, or lack binding to specific data objects and recipients.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node selection is best-effort for repudiation/accountability on publication of data.

title: Presence of deliverable data in the DMZ is detectable
description: The mere existence of files, object counts, sizes, or retrieval readiness indicators in the DMZ can reveal that a research transfer is occurring and may disclose sensitive operational facts about a study, participant cohort, or collaboration, even without direct access to contents.
assumptions: An unauthorized observer can enumerate, probe, or infer repository state through side channels, listings, notifications, or traffic analysis.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit detectability threat for a retrieval-oriented DMZ publication step; PANOPTIC id uncertain.

title: Recipient may be unaware of retention or secondary-use constraints
description: If the delivery mechanism does not convey privacy notices, handling instructions, or usage limitations alongside the research data, the recipient may process or retain the data in ways that exceed participant expectations or agreed constraints.
assumptions: The transfer may omit machine-readable or human-readable policy/consent constraints attached to the dataset.
uncertainty_note: Unawareness applies if contextual notices/constraints are not surfaced during retrieval; PANOPTIC sub-activity is approximate.

title: Unauthorised recipient can retrieve research data from the DMZ
description: Making context-relevant research data available for retrieval from a DMZ creates a risk that an unintended party, or a trusted recipient using the wrong credentials or endpoint, can access the data. This can disclose personal or sensitive research data beyond the intended trusted recipient.
assumptions: The DMZ exposes a retrieval interface or location accessible over a network and holds identifiable or otherwise sensitive research data.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity is a best-effort fit for making data available for recipient retrieval; exact sub-activity id may differ.

title: Recipient can infer additional sensitive attributes from the delivered dataset
description: Even if only context-relevant research data is delivered, the recipient may be able to infer additional attributes, statuses, or relationships about data subjects by combining the dataset with other data already available to them.
assumptions: The delivered dataset contains quasi-identifiers, detailed records, or contextual metadata that can be linked with external information.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity id is best-effort; inference is driven by the retrieval/use of made-available data rather than an explicitly stated analytics step.

title: Delivery artefacts may enable linkability across research deliveries
description: Stable identifiers, file names, transfer metadata, or consistent packaging in the DMZ may allow the recipient or another observer to link multiple deliveries or datasets to the same data subjects, study, or cohort, increasing privacy risk beyond the intended disclosure.
assumptions: Files, manifests, pseudonyms, or transfer metadata remain stable across deliveries or are observable to the recipient.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping; linkability may arise from delivery metadata as well as dataset content.

title: Data subjects may be identifiable in the delivered research data
