description: The context-relevant research data made available in the DMZ may contain direct identifiers or a combination of indirect identifiers sufficient for the trusted recipient to identify individual data subjects, contrary to expectations of minimisation or de-identification.
assumptions: The dataset includes direct identifiers, rare attribute combinations, or granular data that can support re-identification.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity id is approximate; identifiability risk depends strongly on dataset composition and recipient background knowledge.

title: Delivered data may exceed the scope expected by data subjects or agreed research purpose
description: Making data available through the DMZ may involve sharing more fields, records, retention time, or contextual metadata than was consented to, noticed, or contractually permitted, creating a non-compliance risk.
assumptions: There are purpose, consent, contractual, or policy constraints governing what research data may be shared with the recipient.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity is best-effort for data delivery; non-compliance depends on governance and legal basis not fully specified.

title: Data subjects may be unaware their research data is being made available to this recipient
description: The transfer pattern may lack sufficient transparency to data subjects about which trusted recipient can retrieve their context-relevant research data, when it becomes available, and for what exact downstream use.
assumptions: Notices or transparency mechanisms do not fully describe this specific recipient-facing delivery step.
uncertainty_note: Exact LINDDUN tree node and PANOPTIC sub-activity are best-effort due to limited notice/transparency details.

title: Unauthorized retrieval from managed publishing location
description: Research data made available at the NCCoE-managed publishing location may be accessed by parties beyond the intended researchers and trusted interested parties if access control is misconfigured, inherited permissions are too broad, or access tokens/URLs are shared.
assumptions: The publishing location supports access by multiple parties and relies on logical access controls rather than being fully isolated.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity is best-effort; PA03.09 is used to represent making data available for retrieval/publication-like disclosure and may be approximate.

title: Linkability of research subjects or contributors across published datasets
description: If the context-relevant research data contains persistent identifiers, quasi-identifiers, stable pseudonyms, or unique combinations of attributes, recipients retrieving data from the publishing location may link records across releases or with external datasets, revealing relationships about the same individual or group.
assumptions: The shared research data contains repeated or correlatable fields across datasets or over time.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity id is approximate; threat applicability depends on the presence of correlatable attributes in the published data.

title: Inference of sensitive information from context-relevant research data
description: Even when directly identifying fields are absent, authorized recipients may infer sensitive facts about individuals, organizations, or groups by analyzing the released research data alone or in combination with other accessible information.
assumptions: The data includes enough detail, granularity, or auxiliary context to support meaningful inference.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity id is best-effort and may be approximate for this publish/retrieve action.

title: Excessive availability of data beyond intended audience or duration
description: Data placed in the publishing location may remain accessible longer than necessary, be replicated into backups or mirrors, or become reachable to a wider audience than originally intended, increasing the chance of privacy harm from over-disclosure.
assumptions: The publishing location may retain published artifacts, snapshots, or replicated copies beyond the primary sharing event.
uncertainty_note: Tree node selection is best-effort for overexposure via persistent publication; exact PANOPTIC action id is approximate.

title: Insufficient proof of who published or authorized the release
description: If the transfer from the trusted data recipient to the NCCoE-managed publishing location is not strongly logged and bound to the actor's identity and authorization, parties may later dispute who uploaded, approved, or triggered the availability of the research data.
assumptions: Audit logging, identity binding, or approval records for publication may be weak or incomplete.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC action id is approximate; tree node is best-effort for repudiation of publication activity.

title: Unawareness of secondary access and reuse conditions
description: Data subjects or upstream contributors may be unaware that their data is being made available through a managed publishing location to multiple researchers or trusted parties, including the scope of access, downstream reuse, retention, and any redistribution constraints.
assumptions: Not all affected parties have clear notice about this publication channel and its access model.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity is approximate; this threat depends on governance and notice practices outside the flow itself.

title: Publication incompatible with consent or data-sharing restrictions
description: Making the research data available via the publishing location may exceed the permissions, consent terms, contractual restrictions, or policy limitations under which the data was originally collected or shared.
assumptions: The data is subject to consent terms, DUAs, or policy constraints that may not align with this availability model.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC action id is best-effort and may be approximate for this sharing/publication step.

title: Public availability of research data may reveal sensitive personal information
description: Publishing context-relevant research data to an externally managed location can disclose personal data or quasi-identifiers to unintended audiences if the dataset is insufficiently de-identified or contains sensitive attributes.
assumptions: The research data may include personal data, indirect identifiers, or sensitive information, and the publishing location is accessible by researchers and other interested parties beyond the original collection context.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping: PA03.09 is used here to represent making data available/publishing for retrieval, but the exact sub-activity id may differ.

title: Published research data may enable linking back to individuals
description: Even if direct identifiers are removed, releasing the dataset at the publishing location may allow recipients to link records with other available datasets and infer the identity of data subjects.
assumptions: Attackers or legitimate recipients may have access to auxiliary datasets or background knowledge enabling re-identification.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping only; exact PANOPTIC sub-activity id for external publication/disclosure may vary.

title: Publication may be incompatible with the original purpose or consent expectations
description: The trusted data recipient may make research data available to a broader audience than originally expected by data subjects, creating a non-compliance risk if publication is not covered by consent, legal basis, ethics approval, or data-sharing restrictions.
assumptions: Use restrictions, participant expectations, or governance conditions may limit onward publication or broad access.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping: exact sub-activity id is uncertain.

title: Data subjects may be unaware that their data is published in an externally managed location
description: Individuals whose data is included in the research dataset may not be informed that the data is made retrievable from an externally managed publishing platform, reducing transparency about onward disclosure and access conditions.
assumptions: Notice mechanisms may be incomplete, unclear, or absent regarding external publication and downstream access.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping only; exact PANOPTIC sub-activity id uncertain.

title: External publication can expose data subjects to detectability
description: Making the dataset publicly or broadly retrievable can allow an observer to determine whether a specific individual is present in the published dataset, even without fully identifying all records.
assumptions: An adversary may know enough about a target to test for their presence in the released data.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping only; exact PANOPTIC sub-activity id uncertain.

title: Unintended disclosure of sensitive enrollment information in outreach message
description: The outreach attempt tells the patient that a new record has been added to their file. If delivered through an insecure or observable channel (mail, SMS, voicemail, shared email, caller ID context), it may reveal sensitive facts about the patient's prior enrollment or current status to household members, employers, or other third parties.
assumptions: Assumes the outreach channel may be accessible to someone other than the intended patient or that message content is visible before authentication.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity is best-effort; PA05.02 is used here to represent notification/outreach disclosure risk.

title: Patient can be linked to prior enrollment relationship through outreach
description: Receiving a notice from a previous enrollment entity allows observers or intermediaries to infer that the patient has or had a relationship with that organization and that a new file event occurred. This can link the patient across organizational contexts and expose historical participation or case status.
assumptions: Assumes the sender identity or branding is visible to others or inferable from the communication metadata.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping for outreach/notification context; exact sub-activity id may differ.

title: Outreach message enables detectability of patient record creation/update
description: The fact that an outreach attempt occurred may let the patient or third parties detect that a new record was added, even if no further details are provided. This exposes the existence and timing of backend processing activity that the patient may not expect to be externally observable.
assumptions: Assumes message timing/content is sufficient to reveal a backend event.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC id is inferred from a generic notification action; confidence moderate.

title: Insufficient proof of delivery or recipient identity for outreach notification
description: If the previous enrollment entity cannot demonstrate that the outreach reached the correct patient, or the patient can plausibly deny receiving it, disputes may arise about whether notice was properly given. Conversely, the entity may have weak evidence that the intended patient—not another household member—received the message.
assumptions: Assumes the system relies on outreach as meaningful notice and lacks strong authenticated delivery receipts.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC mapping is approximate because the exact sub-activity for notice delivery/audit is uncertain.

title: Patient may be unaware why they were contacted or what data triggered the outreach
description: The notification that a new record was added may not explain what data was added, by whom, from which prior enrollment context, or what consequences follow. This reduces the patient's ability to understand the processing and exercise meaningful control or challenge inaccuracies.
assumptions: Assumes the outreach content is brief and does not provide transparent context or accessible follow-up details.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping for transparency shortcomings in outreach messaging.

title: Inference of sensitive research intent from tool selection
description: The set of bioinformatics tools chosen and the queued job configuration can reveal what kind of sequence analysis is being performed, potentially exposing sensitive hypotheses, disease focus, sample provenance, or subject-related attributes even if raw sequence data are not directly shown in this flow.
assumptions: Assumes tool names, parameters, or pipeline choices are visible to compute-node operators, schedulers, logs, or co-tenants.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity is a best-effort mapping for analyst-driven tool/pipeline selection and job setup; exact id may differ.

title: Identifiability via job metadata and user association
description: Queued jobs may include usernames, project identifiers, dataset references, sample IDs, or persistent job metadata that let the compute environment or its administrators link the analysis request to a specific bioinformaticist, study, or data subject context.
assumptions: Assumes the scheduler or compute platform records submitter identity and job metadata alongside the queued work.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity is best-effort for job submission/queuing metadata handling.

title: Linkability of related analyses across queued jobs
description: Repeated submissions from the same bioinformaticist using similar tools, parameters, dataset references, or queueing patterns may allow the compute platform to correlate multiple jobs and reconstruct a broader analysis campaign or longitudinal study activity.
assumptions: Assumes scheduler logs and job histories are retained and accessible for correlation.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping for submission/queuing activity; exact sub-activity may vary.

title: Insufficient evidence of who queued which tool chain
description: If job submission events, selected tools, and parameter choices are not reliably logged with integrity protection, the organization may be unable to prove who initiated a sensitive analysis or whether a disputed job configuration was actually submitted.
assumptions: Assumes weak audit logging, missing provenance records, or mutable scheduler logs.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping for job queue submission provenance.

title: Unawareness of secondary exposure through queue visibility and logs
description: The bioinformaticist may be unaware that job names, selected tools, parameters, and dataset references entered during queueing are exposed in scheduler dashboards, logs, notifications, or operational telemetry beyond the immediate compute execution context.
assumptions: Assumes shared operational interfaces or broad internal visibility into queued job metadata.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC id is approximate; threat concerns visibility created during job submission and queue management.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of final clinical report to a bioinformaticist
description: The Clinical Result Generation App may provide the final clinical report to a bioinformaticist who is not authorized for this patient or case, exposing sensitive genomic and clinical findings.
assumptions: Bioinformaticists do not automatically have unrestricted need-to-know access to every finalized patient report; access control should be case- and role-scoped.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping only; PA02.06 is used here to represent disclosure/sharing of report data, but the exact sub-activity id may differ.

title: Excessive identifiability through full patient and genomic details in the report
description: The final clinical report may contain direct identifiers and highly distinctive genomic findings, making the patient readily identifiable to the receiving bioinformaticist even where less identifying content would suffice.
assumptions: The report can include direct patient identifiers and/or rare variant information that is inherently identifying.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity id is a best-effort estimate for collection/use of identifying data; exact mapping may vary.

title: Use of finalized report beyond the original clinical purpose
description: Once the bioinformaticist pulls the final report, it could be used for secondary purposes such as research, training, workflow analytics, or case comparison without the patient's expectation or an appropriate legal basis.
assumptions: The workflow or downstream environment may permit retention or reuse of downloaded/fetched reports outside the immediate clinical reporting task.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping for downstream use/processing; exact sub-activity id may differ.

title: Insufficient non-repudiation and auditability of report access
description: If the app does not create reliable audit records for who accessed which final report and when, the organization may be unable to prove or dispute improper access by a bioinformaticist.
assumptions: Audit logging for report retrieval may be incomplete, mutable, or not routinely reviewed.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC id is best-effort for logging/accountability activity; exact sub-activity id may differ.

title: Linkability of patient identity across reports and internal systems
description: The report retrieval may expose stable patient, sample, accession, or case identifiers that allow the bioinformaticist to link this patient across multiple reports, laboratory systems, and datasets beyond what is necessary for the task.
assumptions: Shared identifiers are present in the report or associated retrieval metadata and are reusable across systems.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC mapping is best-effort; PA03.09 is used here to represent cross-context linking, but exact sub-activity id may differ.

title: Local persistence or onward disclosure after report pull
description: After pulling the final clinical report, the bioinformaticist may store, export, print, or forward the report through less controlled channels, increasing the risk of disclosure to unauthorized parties.
assumptions: The receiving workflow may allow download, local caching, screenshots, email forwarding, or printing of the report.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping for transfer/disclosure after retrieval; exact sub-activity id may differ.

title: Sensitive genetic recommendations become visible to unauthorized EMR users
description: Professional recommendations and clinical next steps derived from genetic context are stored in the external EMR, where users beyond the intended care team may be able to access them. This can disclose highly sensitive health and inferred genetic information.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity is best-effort; likely corresponds to recording/storing patient-related data in a clinical system, but exact sub-activity id may differ.

title: Genetic-recommendation entries may enable linkage across care and research contexts
description: Context-relevant research data entered into the external EMR can be correlated with other clinical and administrative records, allowing linkage between a patient's clinical identity, genetic findings, and research participation or research-derived context.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping; exact sub-activity id is uncertain.

title: EMR entry may reveal patient involvement in genetics-related research or evaluation
description: Documenting context-relevant research data and follow-up recommendations in the external EMR may allow readers to infer that the patient underwent genetic assessment, may carry relevant variants, or is associated with a research workflow, even if that fact was not intended to be broadly exposed.
uncertainty_note: Inference focus is confident; exact PANOPTIC sub-activity id is best-effort.

title: Insufficient proof of what recommendation content was entered into the EMR
description: If the transfer from the Genetic Physician to the external EMR lacks strong authorship, timestamping, or immutable audit evidence, it may later be difficult to prove exactly what recommendations or next steps were recorded and by whom.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC mapping is approximate; threat applicability depends on EMR audit controls.

title: Recommendations may be stored longer or more broadly than necessary in the external EMR
description: Once genetic recommendations and clinical next steps are written into the external EMR, they may persist under broad retention policies, backups, and downstream replication, making later deletion or minimization difficult and increasing long-term privacy exposure.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC sub-activity; exact id uncertain.

title: Sensitive genetic recommendations become observable to unauthorized internal users in the EMR
description: When the Genetic Physician records professional recommendations and clinical next steps in the Internal EMR, highly sensitive context-relevant research/genetic information may be disclosed to staff or clinicians who do not need access, especially if role-based access controls, compartmentalization, or break-glass controls are weak.
assumptions: The EMR is accessible by multiple internal roles and the entry includes sensitive genetic or research-related context rather than only minimally necessary treatment metadata.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping for storing/recording sensitive health information in an internal system; exact sub-activity id may vary.

title: EMR entries may enable linkage of genetic recommendations with other clinical records
description: Once genetic recommendations are logged in the Internal EMR, they can be linked with existing demographic, clinical, family-history, and encounter data, allowing a more complete and potentially identifying profile of the patient and their relatives to be assembled.
assumptions: The Internal EMR aggregates longitudinal records and permits querying or viewing across encounters and data domains.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity is a best-effort estimate for linking/combining records; exact id uncertain.

title: Recorded recommendations may make the patient or relatives identifiable through genetic context
description: Even if direct identifiers are minimized in some research-related notes, the combination of rare genetic findings, recommended follow-up actions, family history implications, or specialty context in the EMR may allow identification of the patient or inference about biologically related family members.
assumptions: The stored content contains sufficiently specific genetic or rare-condition context to single out a person or family.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping for identifiability from record content; exact sub-activity id uncertain.

title: Secondary use of recorded genetic recommendations may exceed the original clinical expectation
description: Information entered for immediate care coordination may later be reused inside the organization for research, analytics, operational review, training, or other purposes not fully expected by the patient, creating an unawareness threat regarding downstream processing.
assumptions: The Internal EMR data may be repurposed beyond the immediate treating relationship or the patient was not clearly informed of all downstream internal uses.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping for secondary use/unexpected processing; exact id uncertain.

title: Recording detailed genetic recommendations in the EMR may exceed data minimization or purpose limitation obligations
description: The physician may enter more detail than necessary about research context, familial implications, or speculative genetic interpretations, creating risk that the stored record is not aligned with minimum necessary, purpose limitation, or policy constraints for sensitive genetic information.
assumptions: Applicable organizational policy or law requires minimum necessary handling for sensitive genetic/research data.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping for non-compliant collection/storage detail; exact id uncertain.

title: Insufficient provenance or auditability may impede proving who entered or changed the genetic recommendation
description: If the EMR does not preserve strong timestamps, user attribution, version history, or tamper-evident audit logs for these entries, it may be difficult to demonstrate who recorded, edited, or accessed the recommendation, undermining accountability for sensitive genetic information handling.
assumptions: Audit logging or integrity controls may be incomplete or not routinely reviewed for this data type.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping for accountability/auditability gaps; exact id uncertain.

title: Stored remainder sample may remain identifiable beyond contextual retention need
description: After the technician retrieves or returns the remainder of a physical sample to storage, the sample or its container may still carry direct identifiers or persistent coded labels. If retention requirements have been met, continued storage of an identifiable remainder can enable later association with the individual without sufficient privacy justification.
assumptions: The remainder sample continues to be stored, even though contextual retention requirements for that sample have been met.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping for post-retention storage/retention handling; exact sub-activity id may differ.

title: Remainder sample can be linked back to the data subject through retained labels or codes
description: The stored physical sample may retain labels, accession numbers, barcodes, or other quasi-identifiers that allow personnel or downstream systems to link the remainder sample back to a specific person or record set. This creates linkability even if contextual retention needs have ended.
assumptions: Storage includes a locator, inventory identifier, or other metadata that can be matched to subject records.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping; PANOPTIC sub-activity id is inferred from a retention/storage context.

title: Identity of the sample donor may be inferable from the stored remainder sample
description: Because the sample remains in storage with identifying or easily resolvable metadata, an internal actor who accesses storage records or the sample container may infer the donor's identity. The physical nature of the sample can also increase identifiability where rare sample types or collection contexts are known.
assumptions: Authorized or semi-authorized personnel can access storage areas or related inventory records.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping; exact PANOPTIC sub-activity id uncertain.

title: Insufficient proof that retention limits were evaluated before storing the remainder sample
description: If the technician places the remainder sample back into storage without a reliable audit trail of the retention decision, the organization may later be unable to demonstrate whether the sample should have been destroyed, returned, or further retained. This weakens accountability for privacy-relevant retention handling.
assumptions: Retention decisioning and storage actions are not fully logged or are difficult to correlate.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping to a retention-handling action; exact node may vary depending on the threat-tree granularity used.

title: Storage of the remainder sample may exceed consent or stated retention expectations
description: Once contextual retention requirements have been met, continuing to store the physical remainder may conflict with the individual's consent, notice, or institutional policy regarding how long the sample would be retained. This creates a non-compliance risk tied to the storage step.
assumptions: Applicable consent terms, notices, or policy impose retention limits or purpose limitations for physical samples.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping; exact sub-activity id uncertain without the project-specific PANOPTIC catalog.

title: Residual identifiability from retained disposed-sample records or labels
description: Even after the physical remainder is disposed of, the disposal item/store may retain identifiers, labels, chain-of-custody details, timestamps, or linkage metadata that still allow the sample and its donor/data subject to be identified or re-identified.
assumptions: The disposal item/store records disposal events or preserves labels/metadata rather than representing immediate irreversible destruction with no retained linkage.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping for disposal/destruction activity; exact sub-activity id may differ.

title: Incomplete disposal leaves recoverable physical material
description: If the remainder of the physical sample is not fully destroyed or is placed into a disposal stream that permits retrieval, biological or other sensitive material may remain accessible and disclose personal or health-related information.
assumptions: The physical sample contains potentially sensitive material and disposal may involve intermediate storage or third-party waste handling.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping for disposal/destruction activity; exact sub-activity id may differ.

title: Insufficient proof that disposal occurred as required
description: If the technician does not generate reliable evidence of when, how, and under what authority the sample remainder was disposed, the organization may be unable to demonstrate compliance with retention limits or respond to disputes about whether the sample was actually destroyed.
assumptions: Retention/disposal obligations require auditable proof or attestations of destruction.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping for disposal/destruction activity; exact sub-activity id may differ.

title: Data subjects are unaware of final sample disposal handling
description: The disposal step may occur without the data subject understanding when the physical sample remainder is destroyed, what records about disposal are retained, or whether any exceptions to destruction apply, undermining transparency around the sample lifecycle.
assumptions: The sample relates to an identifiable person and disposal practices are not fully communicated in notices or consent materials.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping for disposal/destruction activity; exact sub-activity id may differ.

title: Residual biological material on reused flow cell can disclose prior sample information
description: If the used flow cell is not adequately cleaned after sequencing, residual physical sample material may remain and be accessible during handling, inspection, maintenance, disposal, or reuse. This can disclose information about a previous individual's sample to unauthorized personnel or contaminate a subsequent run in a way that reveals prior sample presence.
assumptions: The flow cell is reused, handled by multiple staff, or otherwise remains accessible after the original sequencing run; residual sample material can still be recovered or inferred from the device.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping only: PA03.09 is used here to represent post-use retention/cleanup failure leading to residual data exposure; exact sub-activity id may differ.

title: Incomplete decontamination by technician may expose remnants of a physical sample
description: The technician's sample-management action may fail to fully remove biological remnants from the flow cell. That incomplete sanitization creates a disclosure pathway because later users or processes may access leftover material or derive sensitive information from it.
assumptions: Cleaning is manual or partly manual and therefore subject to process gaps, human error, or inadequate validation.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping only: exact PANOPTIC sub-activity for physical media sanitization/decontamination is uncertain.

title: Residual sample on a flow cell can link sequencing runs or individuals
description: Persistent remnants from a prior sample on the used flow cell may allow a later observer or downstream analysis to associate a new sequencing run with a previous individual's material. This creates an unintended link between separate runs, samples, or data subjects.
assumptions: Residual material is detectable and can be associated across runs or handling events.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC action is approximate; linkage here is inferred from cross-run residual sample persistence rather than explicit identifiers.

title: Residual sample material can enable inference of sensitive attributes
description: Even if a subject is not directly identified, biological remnants left on the flow cell may permit inference of sensitive traits, health conditions, ancestry, or other attributes from recovered material or contamination patterns.
assumptions: Adversaries or later handlers have sufficient access and capability to analyze remnants or exploit contamination artefacts.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping only; exact sub-activity id uncertain.

title: Inference of sensitive traits from derived research data stored in the cluster filesystem
description: Context-relevant research data derived from raw sequence data may still encode highly sensitive genomic or health-related attributes. If stored in the cluster filesystem without sufficient minimization or segregation, analysts or other authorized users could infer disease risks, ancestry, kinship, or other sensitive characteristics beyond the immediate research purpose.
assumptions: The derived dataset retains participant-level or otherwise linkable genomic features and is accessible to multiple users or workloads in the cluster environment.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping; PA03.03 is used here for deriving/transforming data into context-relevant research data, but the exact sub-activity id may differ.

title: Re-identification risk from context-relevant research data at rest
description: Even after computation, the resulting research data written to the filesystem may remain directly or indirectly identifying when combined with metadata, sample identifiers, rare variants, timestamps, cohort labels, or external datasets. Storage of these outputs can therefore enable identity inference about data subjects.
assumptions: The output contains participant-level records, rare genomic markers, quasi-identifiers, or stable study metadata that can be linked with other available data.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping; exact PANOPTIC sub-activity id for this transformation/storage step is uncertain.

title: Linkability between derived outputs and original sequence datasets
description: Derived research data persisted in the cluster filesystem may preserve sample IDs, file naming conventions, run identifiers, or stable feature patterns that allow linking the output back to raw sequence files or to other studies involving the same participant. This can undermine dataset separation and increase privacy risk.
assumptions: Identifiers, pseudonyms, consistent file paths, or distinguishing genomic patterns are retained across datasets or processing stages.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC action is a best-effort estimate for the derive/transform step.

title: Excessive derivation of research features beyond necessity
description: The compute nodes may generate richer context-relevant research data than required for the stated research task, such as broad feature sets, secondary annotations, or persistent intermediate results. Over-processing increases the privacy impact because more sensitive information is extracted from the raw sequence data than is necessary.
assumptions: The pipeline can produce optional annotations, intermediate files, or expansive feature matrices that are not strictly needed for the immediate purpose.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping; this is grounded in the processing/derivation activity, but the exact PANOPTIC sub-activity id is uncertain.

title: Use of stored derived data may exceed the original research context or consent boundaries
description: Once context-relevant research data is stored in the shared filesystem, it may later be reused for secondary analyses, broader cohort comparison, model training, or sharing with other project members in ways that are not aligned with the original collection purpose or participant consent constraints.
assumptions: The cluster filesystem supports reuse by multiple teams or workflows and governance controls do not strictly bind later access to the original permitted purpose.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC action chosen as the derivation/output creation step; exact sub-activity id may differ because the privacy issue is amplified by later reuse after storage.

title: Unauthorized portal access exposes final clinical report
description: Uploading the final clinical report to a 3rd party portal creates a risk that unauthorized parties with portal access, compromised credentials, or excessive internal permissions can view sensitive patient information in the report.
assumptions: The final clinical report contains personal and likely sensitive health data, and the 3rd party portal is accessible by multiple parties beyond the uploader.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity is a best-effort estimate for external disclosure/sharing via portal upload; exact sub-activity id may differ.

title: Portal enables use of clinical report beyond original care purpose
description: Once stored on the 3rd party portal, the clinical report may be accessed, reused, or repurposed by the portal provider or other recipients for secondary purposes such as analytics, service improvement, or onward operational use not aligned with the original clinical reporting purpose.
assumptions: The 3rd party portal provider may have technical or contractual ability to access stored reports or related metadata.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping for sharing/upload leading to secondary use; exact PANOPTIC id is uncertain.

title: Upload to third-party portal may occur without adequate patient awareness or valid legal basis
description: Sending the final clinical report to a third-party-hosted portal may not be transparent to the data subject, or may exceed the scope of the consent, notice, or other legal basis under which the report was produced and shared.
assumptions: Patients may not directly interact with or know about the 3rd party portal, and organizational governance for third-party disclosures may be incomplete.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC id is best-effort; legal-basis/transparency issues are contextual and may or may not apply depending on contracts, notices, and healthcare regulations.

title: Portal storage and access patterns may reveal patient involvement
description: Even if report contents are protected, the existence of an uploaded final clinical report, associated identifiers, timestamps, or portal routing metadata may allow observers or portal operators to infer that a specific individual underwent testing or clinical review.
assumptions: The portal stores metadata such as patient identifiers, case IDs, uploader identity, timestamps, or destination information.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping for upload/disclosure metadata; exact node and PANOPTIC sub-activity may vary with the model granularity.

title: Insufficient proof of report upload or recipient access creates repudiation gaps
description: If the upload action is not strongly logged, the bioinformaticist or receiving portal parties may later dispute whether the final clinical report was uploaded, delivered, replaced, or accessed, undermining accountability for the disclosure.
assumptions: Audit logging, integrity protection, and non-repudiation controls for uploads may be limited or inconsistently configured.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC mapping is approximate because this is primarily an accountability issue associated with the upload event.

title: Excessive retention of uploaded clinical reports on the portal
description: The 3rd party portal may retain the final clinical report longer than necessary for the clinical workflow, increasing exposure over time and making later unauthorized access, breach, or secondary use more likely.
assumptions: Retention schedules on the 3rd party portal may not be aligned with data minimization requirements or contractual deletion obligations.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC id is a best-effort estimate for upload/storage leading to retention risk.

title: Unauthorized portal access enables report download by an unauthenticated or weakly authenticated counselor account
description: If the portal session or account used by the Genetic Counselor is not strongly authenticated, an unauthorized person could access the 3rd Party Portal and download the final clinical report, exposing sensitive genetic and clinical information.
assumptions: The download occurs through a user session on the 3rd Party Portal and access control/authentication is required before the report can be retrieved.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping: PA03.02 is used here to represent account/session authentication for portal access; exact sub-activity id may differ.

title: Excessive authorization at the portal allows counselors to download reports beyond their assigned patients
description: The 3rd Party Portal may permit the Genetic Counselor to access or download final clinical reports for individuals outside their treatment relationship or role scope, resulting in unauthorized disclosure of highly sensitive genetic data.
assumptions: The portal stores multiple patient reports and enforces role- or relationship-based access decisions before download.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping: PA03.03 is used to represent authorization/access-decision activity; exact PANOPTIC sub-activity may differ.

title: Report metadata or predictable identifiers allow inference of patient identity or condition before download
description: Even before opening the report, filenames, portal listings, timestamps, accession numbers, or report labels may reveal that a specific person underwent genetic testing or suggest the nature of the clinical finding, enabling inference of sensitive facts.
assumptions: The portal presents report metadata to the user prior to or during download.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping: PA02.01 is used to capture display/exposure of metadata in the retrieval workflow; exact sub-activity id may differ.

title: Downloaded clinical report may be stored insecurely on the counselor endpoint after retrieval
description: Once downloaded, the final clinical report may reside in browser download folders, temporary files, synced drives, or unmanaged local storage on the Genetic Counselor's device, increasing the chance of later unauthorized access or secondary disclosure.
assumptions: The workflow involves a file download to an endpoint or client environment controlled by or accessible to the counselor.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC action is a best-effort mapping to local storage/retention after download; exact sub-activity id may differ.

title: Insufficient download logging undermines accountability for access to final clinical reports
description: If the 3rd Party Portal does not create reliable, tamper-resistant audit records for who downloaded which final clinical report and when, inappropriate access may be difficult to investigate or contest, weakening accountability for sensitive data handling.
assumptions: The portal is expected to log report access and download events.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping: PA03.08 is used to represent audit/logging of retrieval events; exact sub-activity id may differ.

title: Portal interface may not make the sensitivity and downstream handling implications of the report clear at download time
description: The counselor may download a final clinical report without clear contextual cues about special handling requirements, scope limitations, or whether particularly sensitive genetic findings are included, reducing user awareness and increasing the risk of mishandling.
assumptions: The portal UI is the primary interface through which the counselor selects and downloads the report.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping to user-facing presentation during retrieval; exact sub-activity id may differ, and applicability depends on portal UX.

title: Unnecessary exposure of context-relevant research/genetic data to clinician
description: The Genetic Counselor may make more context-relevant research or genetic data available than is necessary for the Clinician's immediate care task, enabling access to sensitive inferred health and familial information beyond the intended purpose.
assumptions: The shared dataset may include rich research-derived or genetic context rather than a minimally necessary subset.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping for making data available/retrievable with added analysis; exact sub-activity id may differ.

title: Linkability of research-derived data with clinician-held patient records
description: When the Clinician retrieves and combines the context-relevant research data with additional clinical input and analysis, the data may become linkable to broader patient records, increasing the ability to correlate identities, conditions, and events across contexts.
assumptions: The clinician environment contains other identifiable patient data or longitudinal records that can be combined with the retrieved data.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity is a best-effort estimate for retrieval/combination and may not exactly match the canonical id.

title: Secondary use of genetic/research data during clinician analysis
description: The Clinician's additional input and analysis may use the made-available research/genetic data for purposes beyond the original context for which the Genetic Counselor exposed it, such as broader diagnostic speculation, teaching, or onward sharing within care operations.
assumptions: Purpose limitation and use constraints are not technically enforced at retrieval or analysis time.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping for downstream use/analysis; exact sub-activity id uncertain.

title: Identification of patient or relatives from genetic context during retrieval and analysis
description: Even if the shared data is partially de-identified, the Clinician may be able to identify the patient or family members by combining genetic context, rare variants, pedigree clues, and existing clinical knowledge.
assumptions: Data includes genomic or pedigree-related attributes that are highly identifying in context.
uncertainty_note: Tree node chosen as a general identifiability threat; exact PANOPTIC id is best effort.

title: Insufficient transparency to patient about clinician access and analysis of research-context data
description: The patient may not be aware that context-relevant research data made available by the Genetic Counselor can be retrieved by the Clinician and further analyzed with new inputs, reducing awareness of how their sensitive data is disclosed and used.
assumptions: Patient-facing notices or consent artifacts do not clearly describe this specific access path and analysis activity.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping; precise sub-activity uncertain.

title: Processing of sensitive genetic/research data without adequately aligned consent or legal basis
description: The Clinician's retrieval and further analysis of research-derived genetic/contextual data may exceed the scope of the patient's consent or other authorized basis, especially where research and care contexts are governed differently.
assumptions: Research-originated data is subject to context-specific consent, access, or governance restrictions.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping for retrieval/use under potentially misaligned authorization; exact sub-activity id uncertain.

title: Residual genomic data remains on wet lab devices after decommissioning
description: If storage on privacy-relevant wet lab devices is not fully sanitized during decommissioning, genomic or related metadata may remain recoverable by subsequent owners, service providers, or recyclers, causing unintended disclosure.
assumptions: The devices contain persistent local storage, caches, logs, or embedded memory that may store genomic data or associated metadata.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping: likely falls under a data disposal/sanitization sub-activity, but the exact PANOPTIC sub-activity id may differ.

title: Lack of auditable proof that device sanitization was completed before resale
description: If the decommissioning specialist does not produce reliable records of wiping, destruction, or verification steps, the organization may be unable to demonstrate that privacy-preserving decommissioning occurred, weakening accountability and making disputes about prior exposure hard to resolve.
assumptions: Decommissioning includes procedural steps that should be logged or certified before devices are released or resold.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping: likely related to disposal/sanitization. Tree node is approximate because repudiation coverage depends on how evidence of decommissioning is modeled.

title: Recoverable device configuration or metadata reveals prior genomic processing context
description: Even if primary files are removed, retained logs, configuration data, user identifiers, network settings, sample identifiers, or run histories on the device can reveal sensitive information about data subjects, projects, or the organization that processed genomic data.
assumptions: The devices store operational metadata beyond the primary genomic datasets.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping: likely a decommissioning/sanitization activity, but exact PANOPTIC sub-activity id is uncertain.

title: Residual genomic or device-usage data remains on acquired/refurbished wet-lab devices
description: If a wet-lab device is acquired from a third party or inadequately refurbished, prior owners' sensitive digital data (for example genomic runs, sample identifiers, user accounts, logs, or network settings) may remain on the device and become accessible to the acquiring organization, causing disclosure of personal or otherwise sensitive information.
assumptions: The device contains non-volatile storage or embedded logs/configuration that can persist across ownership changes.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping only; PA01.02 is used here to represent residual-data exposure during acquisition/refurbishment and may be approximate.

title: Procurement without privacy validation can introduce devices that leak data to unauthorized parties
description: If the Device Acquisition Specialist procures devices without validating manufacturer provenance, refurbishment quality, secure wipe status, and privacy-preserving configuration, the acquired device may later disclose genomic or operational data through retained storage, insecure defaults, or unauthorized remote access channels.
assumptions: The acquisition process includes selection and acceptance of devices and can require privacy/security attestations from vendors or refurbishers.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity is a best-fit estimate for privacy-related acquisition/acceptance checks and may be approximate.

title: Retained identifiers on refurbished devices enable linking to prior data subjects or organizations
description: Persistent serial-linked records, account data, instrument names, or embedded sample metadata on refurbished devices can allow the new owner or service personnel to link the device to prior patients, samples, operators, or institutions, revealing relationships that should not transfer with the equipment.
assumptions: The device stores identifiers or metadata that survive refurbishment and are readable after acquisition.
uncertainty_note: PA03.09 is a best-effort match for identifier/metadata persistence enabling linkage; exact PANOPTIC sub-activity may differ.

title: Acquisition from manufacturer/refurbisher may occur without adequate notice or contractual controls over residual personal data
description: Personal data left on the device by previous users may be transferred to the acquiring organization without those individuals being informed and without contractual restrictions governing such transfer, undermining awareness and policy compliance expectations around downstream processing.
assumptions: Previous operators or data subjects are not informed that device resale/refurbishment can transfer embedded personal data.
uncertainty_note: LINDDUN mapping to non-compliance is best-effort because the exact applicable legal/contractual context is not provided; PANOPTIC id is approximate.
